\chapter{Review --- Five Sets, Finished}
\label{ch:repaso-parejas}
\hlchaptermodality{256}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use every one of the sets the book had left half-taught.}

I can use every one of the sets the book had left half-taught.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{(review)}

\label{lesson:ES-C65-repaso-parejas}



\begin{quote}
Three places, in order. (\emph{Aquí}, \emph{ahí}, \emph{allí}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five chants, and each one finishes something.

\textbf{Places.} \emph{Aquí}, \emph{\textbf{ahí}}, \emph{\textbf{allí}} — one for each of \emph{este}, \emph{ese}, \emph{aquel}.

\textbf{Times.} \emph{\textbf{Ahora}}, \emph{\textbf{hoy}}, \emph{mañana} — now, today, tomorrow.

\textbf{Articles.} \emph{Un libro}, \emph{\textbf{unos}} \emph{libros} — one, then a few.

\textbf{Possessives.} \emph{Nuestra casa}, \emph{\textbf{vuestra}} \emph{casa} — and with that the set of six is closed.

\textbf{Two verbs.} \emph{\textbf{Vi}}, \emph{\textbf{di}} — the shortest pasts in the language.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a gap in a set is hard to see}]
Every one of these was a set you already partly had. You had \emph{aquí} without \emph{ahí}. You had \emph{mañana} without \emph{hoy}. You had \emph{un} without \emph{unos}, and \emph{nuestro} without \emph{vuestro}.

That is a particular kind of gap, and it is harder to notice than a missing subject, because nothing feels absent — you simply use the half you have and route around the rest.

And two small rules came out of it worth keeping. \emph{Vi} and \emph{di} take \textbf{no accent}, because a one-syllable word has nowhere else the beat could fall. And \emph{dar}, though an \emph{-ar} verb, takes the \emph{-er} endings in the past.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the five chants, in order
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many possessives are in the closed set? (\textbf{Six.})

And which place word matches \emph{ese}? (\emph{\textbf{Ahí}} — the listener's side.)
\end{tcolorbox}
